newsitem.title: POLAND: POLES SUPPORT NEW CONSTITUTION, POLL SHOWS.
newsitem.headline: POLES SUPPORT NEW CONSTITUTION, POLL SHOWS.

text.p: Poles are likely to approve a new constitution draft in a nationwide referendum on May 25, despite opposition from rightist groups outside parliament, a public opinion poll showed on Tuesday.
The poll by the private Demoskop agency indicated that 55 percent of those planning to vote would back the draft, 14 percent were against it, while 31 percent were still undecided.
The poll suggested turnout at the referendum was likely to be 66 percent.

Some analysts see the referendum as a test of strength before the general election, due around September, between the ruling coalition dominated by ex-communists and Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) which is seeking to enter parliament.
The AWS and other rightist groups have urged Poles to reject the new charter, saying it is too secular.

Recent opinion polls show the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the AWS, a bloc of more than 30 small parties led by the Solidarity trade union, are running neck-in-neck with support of between 20 and 29 percent.
If approved, the new constitution would replace the 1952 Stalin-era one and an interim charter adopted as a stopgap after the fall of communism in 1989.

The draft is supported by the government coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party along with two opposition parties in parliament. The groups reached a difficult compromise on the charter after nearly four years of work.

The constitution draft slightly weakens the presidency, with parliament allowed to overthrow the president's veto by three-fifths of votes in the lower house, rather than the present two-thirds majority.
It bans fascist, communist and racist political parties.

Many economists hail the new constitution for banning the government from financing the budget deficit in the central bank and from increasing the public debt to more than 60 percent of gross domestic product.
The early April poll by Demoskop was carried out among a representative sample of 994 people. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
